extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners working with PCT procedures (particularly PRH users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing and handling international search reports (ISR), written opinions (WO), supplementary/ITS searches (SIS/ITS), IPEA Demands and the IPEA preliminary opinion (IPER) under the PCT framework, including required forms, contents, timing, language, unity, fees and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending ISR when new publications appear
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant publications become known after ISR has been prepared, a new (amended) ISR is to be prepared and marked 'amended'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably amendments should be made before the IB has completed technical preparations for publication. Amendments may be made up to two years from the priority date (or international filing date if no priority). A copy of the corrected report is sent to the applicant and to the IB. (ISPE GL 15.74)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and form of ISA written opinion (WO)
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA prepares a written opinion (WO) simultaneously with the ISR, using form PCT/ISA/237 in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepared under Rule 43bis and ISPE GL 17; the WO is produced together with the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for the written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion is prepared on the basis of the original application or the translation supplied for ISA examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WO content and findings must be based on the version of the application available to ISA (original or accepted translation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive matters WO must address
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA's written opinion must state whether the invention is new, involves an inventive step, and is industrially applicable, and whether the international application meets the requirements of the PCT and its Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WO should indicate parts of the application that are deficient and which PCT articles/rules the application fails to comply with, either by reference or clear reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion structure: use of Box sheets (I–VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The WO (form PCT/ISA/237) comprises a cover sheet and box sheets Box No. I–VIII and supplemental sheets; only those sheets needed are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each box sheet is used for specific types of information (see separate box-specific criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box I — Basis documents indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. I indicates which documents the written opinion is based on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet and the box indicating the basis of the opinion must be included; only needed sheets are attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box II — Priority remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority-related remarks are presented on Box No. II; the box is not filled if no priority was claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all cited prior art in the ISR became public before the earliest priority date, Box II is not filled and validity of priority is not examined. If any cited publication became public after the earliest priority, priority validity is assessed. If priority documents/translations are not available, opinion is drafted assuming priority valid, but if priority is found invalid this is stated and justified. P-category publications are considered when assessing novelty and inventive step if priority invalid. (ISPE GL 6, 17.28–17.31)

rubrics_metrics.name: Box III — No opinion on novelty/inventiveness/industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. III is used when the WO takes no position on novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where ISA/IPEA does not examine these matters for certain claims or overall (as per applicable rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box IV — Lack of unity (non-unity) indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. IV is used to indicate that the invention is not unitary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application lacks unity this is recorded and reasons provided. This affects which claims are examined/searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box V — Reasoned opinion on novelty/inventiveness/industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. V contains a reasoned statement on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, usually covering all claims that were the subject of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications may examine closest prior art publications, explain how the invention differs from the prior art; full bibliographic details of cited documents are in the ISR. Third-party observations timely submitted may be taken into account; referenced publications in such observations need not be mentioned unless the ISA considers it necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VI — Special cited documents (exceptional prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. VI lists special cited publications that are public before the international filing date or earliest priority date and therefore are not considered part of the prior art under Rule 64.1, along with their categorisation (E, O or P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes patent applications, utility model applications and grants that were public on the filing/priority date. State publication date, filing date and priority date. ISA may note if it considers a listed publication's priority invalid. If the list is long, reference to the ISR can replace full listing. Non-written disclosures (presentations, public use, exhibitions) relevant to the invention and their documentary evidence and dates should also be indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VII — Specific deficiencies in the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. VII is used to report deficiencies in the content or form of the international application not addressed elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT Articles and Rules define specific formal and substantive requirements (e.g. Rule 5.1(a)(ii) for insufficient description of the prior art). Such deficiencies should be referenced to the applicable rule when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VIII — Specific remarks on the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. VIII is used for special remarks regarding the international application, such as unclear claims, description or drawings or claims insufficiently supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such remarks must be substantiated/reasoned in the WO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 19 amendments to claims after ISA stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 19 the applicant has one opportunity to amend claims in the international phase; amended claims must be sent to the IB in the publication language and are published with the PCT application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: amendments available until 16 months from priority or until 2 months from the date of sending the ISA results, whichever is later. If some claims were not examined, Article 19 amendments can only be made to claims that were examined. Applicant must submit all claim pages replacing earlier pages and a letter indicating differences and grounds for the changes; amendments are free of charge. If Demand is filed, Article 19 amendments are forwarded to IPEA; applicant may also amend under Article 34 during the IPEA phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal comments to the International Bureau (IB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may file informal comments only to the IB in the publication language during the international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal comments must be submitted within 30 months (preferably 28 months) from the earliest priority date. IB does not forward such comments to an IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-Type Search (ITS) — scope and no written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA may perform an International-Type Search (ITS) for a national patent application (form PCT/ISA/201); ITS includes only a search and no written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ITS request must be made to the patent office in writing within 3 months of the filing date, with the required fee and any required translation into the ISA-approved language. PRH checks formal requirements and forwards the request to the selected ISA. The ITS report is typically ready in 4–5 months and its content largely corresponds to PCT/ISA/210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ITS results in national prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: ITS results are part of the national application file and are used to limit the scope of national examination, but the national examiner is not bound by the international searcher's conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no justified reason to depart, ITS outcome is taken as a starting point for national examination. ITS search and response become public with other application documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary International Search (SIS) — general rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: SIS is based on Rule 45bis; applicant may request SIS from any PCT authority that performs such searches except the authority that carried out the original ISA; SIS must be started immediately or by 22 months from earliest priority and the SISR must be completed by 28 months from earliest priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SISR does not include a written opinion (WO) but may include explanations about the scope of the SIS and the cited documents considered relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIS unity and limits of SIS search
rubrics_metrics.description: SISR is prepared only for the part of the international application covering one single invention (typically the invention first mentioned in the claims). SIS does not provide for paid additional searches for other inventions excluded for lack of unity in the ISA stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may request in the request form (PCT/IB/375 Box IV) that the SIS be limited to an invention excluded in ISA due to lack of unity. SISA is not obliged to search parts left out by the earlier ISA. If SIS limits search for lack of unity, applicant can request review within one month; if the SISA panel finds the restriction unjustified a new SISR covering the full application is prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: SISR content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SISR (form PCT/SISA/501) comprises first and second sheets and optional annexes; the first sheet indicates documents on which the report is based and whether the ISA ISR/WO were available; the second sheet is similar to PCT/ISA/210 but without classification data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First sheet notes if some claims were not examined and whether the invention is non-unitary; a 'Scope Annex' can describe the search scope and is useful if earlier ISA report not available to SISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: When SISR is not prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: SISA does not prepare an SISR (and issues declaration PCT/SISA/502) if all claims relate to subject matter ISA is not required to search, or if explanation/claims/drawings prevent a meaningful search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is made on PCT/SISA/502 and sent with form PCT/SISA/505 to applicant and IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand (IPEA request) filing channels and initial checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand may be filed electronically via PRH systems, by email, paper, or in person; PRH issues an automatic receipt for electronic submissions and performs a formal check of the Demand and its attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH verifies selection of PRH as IPEA (or forwards to IB or chosen EPO/Sweden if other IPEA chosen), sends required forms to IB and calculates deadlines. Demand deadline: 22 months from earliest priority or three months from ISR mailing, whichever is later. If filed after 19 months from priority, IB is informed on form PCT/RO/402.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to indicate for IPEA examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must indicate on form PCT/IPEA/401 which documents are to be the basis for IPEA examination; PRH reviews the form and attachments and the chosen language for IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amended pages for IPEA were not supplied with the Demand, PRH will request them using PCT/IPEA/431. If fees missing or incomplete, PRH issues PCT/IPEA/403 giving one month to pay; late payment incurs surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA fees and payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA-stage fees are payable to the investigating patent office according to the selected authority's fee schedule; at least the handling fee and the IPEA search/examination fee must be paid with the Demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees are not paid in time PRH sends a notice (PCT/IPEA/403) and the applicant has one month to pay. Failure to pay may delay or prevent transfer to an examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPER purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA's purpose is to prepare a preliminary, non-binding opinion (IPER) on whether the invention(s) are new, involve an inventive step and are industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA will take positions only on claims that were the subject of an ISA search. Nevertheless, the IPEA must consider all relevant material whether or not it was mentioned in the ISR (Article 33(6); Rule 70.7). IPEA may carry out a top-up search for publications after the ISR date unless such top-up is unnecessary (e.g. where Rule 67.1 excludes consideration or application is too unclear to allow meaningful search). IPEA also considers timely third-party observations provided supporting documents are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA start and IPER deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA can start once formalities are complete, required fees are paid, and ISA results are available, unless applicant requested postponement; IPER must be ready by the latest of: 28 months from earliest priority (or filing if no priority), 6 months from the IPEA start date defined by Rule 69.1, or 6 months from the date IPEA received any translation under Rule 55.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may request postponement of start to the Rule 69.1(d) date or to the Rule 54bis.1(a) date if desired (see rules cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and language bases for IPEA examination
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA examines the documents indicated in PCT/IPEA/401 and handles languages per PRH practice: Finnish, Swedish and English are accepted; if original was Finnish/Swedish but applicant chose English for the IPEA, the English publication (WO) or Article 19/34 documents are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPEA will process Finnish/Swedish originals only if the applicant selected those languages and originals are the filing documents. Applicant may indicate whether the IPEA should start based on originals, Article 19 amended documents, or Article 34 amended documents; applicant may also request Article 19 amendments be considered cancelled. If IPEA receives copies of amendments before it starts the written opinion/IPER, those are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity objection and extra-fee procedure in IPEA (PCT/IPEA/405)
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple independent inventions are present and their examination would cause significant extra work, IPEA requests restriction to one invention or payment of additional fees using form PCT/IPEA/405, giving one month to respond or pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PCT/IPEA/405 details which claim combinations would be unitary and for which invention IPEA will perform the search if the applicant does not respond/pay. Applicant may pay the extra fees and file a protest against the request, with the protest handled by a reviewing body; PRH charges no fee for protest handling. If the IPEA deadline cannot be met due to lack of unity, IPER is made once fees are paid or deadline for payment lapses. If the IPEA and ISA are the same authority and the same examiner performed both, the examiner normally does both searches unless there is reason to diverge.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA written opinion content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA's written opinion (form PCT/IPEA/408, English) should address matters specified in Rule 66.2 and Article 34(4), including missing matters defined in Article 34(4), lack of novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability, formal/content deficiencies that IPEA examines, changes introducing matter not present in the original, claims not sufficiently supported by the description, claims not searched because ISA did not search them, and sequence listing format issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form includes a cover sheet and Box No. I–VIII plus sequence listing annexes; include only the sheets needed. Box descriptions correspond to the ISA boxes (see ISA WO box guidance). The response deadline for the applicant to the written opinion is generally two months from the mailing date (min 1 month, max 3 months) and can be extended if applicant requests before expiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of conclusions in IPEA written opinion and IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA's written opinion should indicate whether IPER will be negative for any claim; if all claims are deemed new, inventive and industrially applicable, the IPER will be positive and Box V need not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Rule 66.2 the examiner may limit Box V to the claims that fail the criteria rather than restating positive findings for all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to issue a written opinion vs proceed directly to IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has not seriously attempted to correct deficiencies noted in ISA WO, the examiner may proceed directly to drafting IPER without issuing a new written opinion; if applicant has tried but the application still fails requirements, the examiner may issue a new WO provided there is enough time to prepare IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IPEA top-up search finds new relevant publications, the IPEA should give a written opinion. Multiple written opinions may be provided at IPEA discretion and if deadlines permit. Applicant can be given opportunity for further amendments and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal communications between IPEA and applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA may at any time communicate informally with the applicant or their representative by writing, phone or meeting and may record such communications in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISPE GL 19.41-19.46 give guidance on informal contacts and how to record their substance and any changes to the file arising from them (Rule 66.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to reply to a written opinion and effect of non-response
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's reply time is usually two months from the WO mailing date (not less than one month and not more than three months). Extensions can be granted if requested before expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not reply in time, IPEA will prepare IPER based on available documents. Late replies may be considered unless IPER already prepared; under Rule 66.4bis IPEA need not take into account changes or arguments submitted after it has begun drafting the written opinion or IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA top-up search policy
rubrics_metrics.description: IPEA may perform an additional (top-up) search for documents published or made known after ISR preparation unless IPEA considers such top-up unnecessary (e.g., if Rule 67.1 indicates no substantive opinion is to be given, if the application is too unclear to permit meaningful search, or if no claims were searched in ISA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-up search is unnecessary if the entire claim set is not to be considered on novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability, or if the claims cannot be meaningfully researched because of lack of clarity or lack of support. If top-up finds new relevant publications, a written opinion should be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPER notification and document handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When IPER is completed the IPEA sends form PCT/IPEA/409 and a notice PCT/IPEA/416 to IB and the applicant; PRH also forwards all documents supplied during the IPEA stage, including earlier amended pages and applicant letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures IB and applicant have the complete IPEA-stage record.
